themes_detail.label: Tree Hazard Spike
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree and branch complaints surged to 3 THIS WEEK compared to a 0.2-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1100% spike (z-score: 6.35)—suggesting sudden seasonal growth or deferred maintenance creating public safety risks across Washington Heights/Inwood.
evidence: 3 overgrown tree/branch complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Parks safety and park reconstruction are repeated unfunded budget requests from community board, indicating chronic underinvestment
Spike emerged in final week of spring, coinciding with rapid foliage growth season
reporting_angles: Interview residents about blocked sidewalks or fallen branches; verify if Parks Dept has staffing/budget constraints for trimming
Check Parks Dept tree maintenance schedules and compare complaint hotspots to deferred work orders

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 23 LAST WEEK versus a 3.8-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 513% spike (z-score: 6.03)—indicating a rapid escalation of visible homelessness and street conditions in the district.
evidence: 23 encampment complaints last week vs. 3.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (513% spike, z-score 6.03)
Community board repeatedly requests enhanced park safety and more security staff, suggesting underlying service gaps
Food assistance (SNAP/Food Stamps) is a chronic unfunded budget priority, indicating possible economic stress drivers
reporting_angles: Canvass affected neighborhoods (likely parks, subway areas) to locate encampments; interview residents and service providers about what triggered the sudden increase
Contact NYPD Homeless Outreach Unit and Department of Social Services to understand if there was a triggering event (shelter closure, policy change, weather) last week

themes_detail.label: Sanitation Service Breakdown
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints surged to 13 LAST WEEK compared to a 3.4-complaint weekly average over 8 weeks (285% spike, z-score 3.93), while sanitation worker/vehicle complaints hit 3 TWO WEEKS AGO versus 0.5 baseline (500% spike, z-score 3.54), suggesting systemic failures in sanitation operations.
evidence: 13 street sweeping complaints last week vs. 3.4 weekly average (285% spike, z-score 3.93)
3 sanitation worker/vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (500% spike, z-score 3.54)
Community board has repeatedly requested more frequent litter basket collection—an unfunded, multi-year request signaling chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Request Department of Sanitation district-level staffing and route data; determine if there were recent layoffs, route consolidations, or equipment failures
Interview residents on specific blocks about street conditions; photograph uncollected litter and compare to service schedules

themes_detail.label: Bike Abandonment Spike
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO from a 0.2-complaint weekly baseline (1100% increase, z-score 6.35), suggesting either a sudden influx of dockless bikes or a new enforcement/complaint awareness pattern in the district.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Spike timing suggests possible new bike-share deployment or seasonal increase in abandoned rentals
High z-score indicates statistically unusual event rather than normal variation
reporting_angles: Verify if a bike-share operator (Citi Bike, Lime, etc.) recently expanded service into Washington Heights/Inwood or changed fleet management
Canvass neighborhoods to locate clustered abandoned bikes and photograph them; contact operators about removal protocols

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk Deterioration Pattern
themes_detail.summary: Sidewalk condition complaints hit 21 THREE WEEKS AGO versus a 5.8-complaint weekly average (265% spike, z-score 6.01), aligning with community board's repeated requests for street and park infrastructure upgrades, suggesting deferred maintenance is creating visible hazards.
evidence: 21 sidewalk condition complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 5.8 weekly average (265% spike, z-score 6.01)
Community board has made repeated, unfunded budget requests for park and street reconstruction for multiple years
Fatal fire story (THE CITY, May 2026) mentioned landlords racking up 1000+ violations—possible indicator of broader building/infrastructure neglect in area
reporting_angles: Map the 21 sidewalk complaints geographically; conduct street audit of those blocks, photographing trip hazards, broken pavement, and uneven surfaces
Contact Department of Transportation about repair backlogs and budget allocation to Community District 112; compare to other districts
